title: PSR-W3: Regev-type streaming collimation with three levels (b = ceil(n/3)) - polynomial memory, polynomial source copies O(n^5), time 2^(n/3) poly(n)

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR-W3 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md (Regev-type streaming combiner with b = ceil(n/3) label bits collimated per level, so at most three levels, r = b + 1 child qubits per node) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its total charged sequential work satisfies T(N,s) = O(n^9 2^(n/3)), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n^9 2^(n/3) and exact growth index 1. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR-W3 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md (Regev-type streaming combiner with b = ceil(n/3) label bits collimated per level, so at most three levels, r = b + 1 child qubits per node) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its peak classical workspace in bits satisfies S_C(N,s) = O(n^2), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n^2 and exact growth index 0. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR-W3 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md (Regev-type streaming combiner with b = ceil(n/3) label bits collimated per level, so at most three levels, r = b + 1 child qubits per node) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its peak quantum workspace in qubits satisfies S_Q(N,s) = O(n), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n and exact growth index 0. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single capped PSR-W3 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md (Regev-type streaming combiner with b = ceil(n/3) label bits collimated per level, so at most three levels, r = b + 1 child qubits per node) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 3/4 from independent ideal coset copies. On every execution branch its total acquired source copies, including all discards and failed attempts, satisfy Q(N,s) = O(n^5), uniformly with absolute constants, with the uniform bit-length representative envelope B(n) = n^5 and exact growth index 0. This holds jointly with all other resource claims and the clean-input tolerance below for the same algorithm, including all failures, restarts, cutoff branches, source costs, controller bit operations, addressing and precision costs as applicable.

For the same capped PSR-W3 algorithm and fixed configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, the proved fractional tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: every acquired source copy is independent and ideal. Under this promise full-secret recovery succeeds with unconditional probability at least 3/4 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance or impossibility of greater tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
